KNITPASS - Deliverable D2.1
Data model for digital product passports in knitwear
Work package 2 - Version 1.0 - Public - 28 February 2025

1. Summary
This deliverable defines the data model for a digital product passport (DPP) for knitwear.
It lists 42 data points grouped in six blocks: identity, materials, production steps,
use and care, repair, and end of life. For each data point it states whether small and
medium-sized knitwear makers already hold the data, and which source can provide it.

2. Why knitwear needs its own passport profile
Knitted garments are often made in small batches, with yarns bought from several spinners
and dyed in separate lots. The Ecodesign for Sustainable Products Regulation (ESPR)
requires passports for textiles once the delegated act applies. Traceability of yarn lots
is the hardest part for small producers.

3. Data points
Identity: GTIN or internal article number, batch number, production country.
Materials: fibre composition by weight, recycled content, yarn spinner, yarn lot number.
Production steps: knitting technique (flat, circular, whole garment), dyeing method,
finishing chemicals, factory location.
Use and care: washing temperature, drying, pilling class.
Repair: spare yarn availability, repair service contact role.
End of life: take-back scheme, sorting code, recyclability score.

4. Open template
An open spreadsheet template and a JSON schema implementing this model are published with
this deliverable. The pilot knitters in the Netherlands and Portugal filled in passports
for 120 styles in three months.
